definitions.gloss: world of difference; vast gap; enormous disparity
definitions.explanation: An extremely large difference between two things, likened to the distance between clouds and mud — the highest and lowest things imaginable.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{実力|じつりょく}には{雲泥|うんでい}の{差|さ}がある。
examples.english: There is a world of difference in ability between the two.

examples.japanese: {去年|きょねん}と{今年|ことし}の{成績|せいせき}には{雲泥|うんでい}の{差|さ}がある。
examples.english: There is a vast difference between last year's and this year's results.

examples.japanese: {手作|てづく}りのケーキと{市販|しはん}のケーキでは、{味|あじ}に{雲泥|うんでい}の{差|さ}がある。
examples.english: There is a world of difference in taste between a homemade cake and a store-bought one.

notes:
An idiomatic expression combining {雲|うん} (clouds) and {泥|でい} (mud) — the most distant extremes — with {差|さ} (difference). The image is that two things are as far apart as the sky and the ground.

ETYMOLOGY:
From classical Chinese, comparing the distance between clouds (the highest) and mud (the lowest). The standalone compound {雲泥|うんでい} already means "vast difference," and adding の{差|さ} makes this explicit.

USAGE:
Almost always used in the pattern ～には{雲泥|うんでい}の{差|さ}がある (there is a world of difference in ~). Can describe positive or negative comparisons.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天|てん}と{地|ち}ほどの{差|さ} — difference as great as heaven and earth (similar meaning)
- {月|つき}とすっぽん — comparing the moon and a snapping turtle (two things that look similar but are vastly different in quality)
- {大|おお}きな{差|さ} — big difference (plain, non-idiomatic)
